mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates do not rise.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when accompanied by strong corporate profit growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5 percentage points signals an emergency monetary easing, which immediately boosts risk asset valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails outside of crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a statistical artifact or large-scale labor force reclassification, which historically coincides with short-term S&P 500 volatility and negative returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the pattern does not recur in at least 3 out of the last 5 such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 1.5% signals weakening consumer demand, which is associated with lower earnings revisions and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of strong export growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes when export growth is also strong.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -0.5% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply shock, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of falling energy prices.
